raw_answer_text:
Topology genre needs `reference/experimental/topology.md` and `reference/layout.md`, per the router table — neither was included in the documentation I was given, so the exact node/edge keyword spellings below are my best-faith composition from the core grammar (quoted labels, bare ids, `class` for meaning) rather than a verified lookup. Per "Do not invent syntax," please run `node build-svg.js branch-office-wan.fd` before treating this as final — if the genre file spells devices/links differently, the build will name the correct replacement and I'll fix it in one pass.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

class wan "WAN uplink" stroke=#2563eb
class backup "Backup path" stroke=#dc2626 style=dashed

switch access1 "Access Switch 1"
switch access2 "Access Switch 2"
router branch "Branch Router"
router hubprimary "Primary Hub Router"
router hubbackup "Backup Hub Router"

link access1 branch
link access2 branch
link branch hubprimary class=wan
link branch hubbackup class=wan,backup
```

Notes on the source, kept out of the figure itself:
- The description gives no bandwidth, carrier, or interface detail for any link — nothing was invented to fill that gap; the figure states only what was given (endpoints, and primary vs. backup role).
- `wan`/`backup` classes exist so the primary-vs-backup distinction reads from the render itself, not just the label text — per the "class is how meaning survives" rule, since color/dash alone would assert nothing a reader could recover otherwise.
- access1–branch and access2–branch are plain access links (no class), since the source didn't characterize them beyond "connected."
